handoff.purpose: Implements the session event stream, line/typed-event parsing, and lifecycle control for a one-shot subprocess adapter.

symbols.name: _parse_line
symbols.note: Parses a single output line into an AgentEvent; falls back to TextDelta on JSON parse failure or non-dict payloads.

symbols.name: _parse_typed_event
symbols.note: Maps an event_type string and data dict to specific AgentEvent subclasses; unknown types become a system-role AgentMessage.

symbols.name: approve
symbols.note: Always raises NotImplementedError; no approval protocol for one-shot CLI profiles.

symbols.name: reject
symbols.note: Always raises NotImplementedError; no rejection protocol for one-shot CLI profiles.

symbols.name: interrupt
symbols.note: Sends SIGINT to the session process if it is still running; swallows ProcessLookupError and OSError.

symbols.name: _stop_process
symbols.note: Static helper that terminates a process, waits up to 5s, then kills if needed; swallows ProcessLookupError and OSError.

symbols.name: terminate
symbols.note: Pops session and sequence, stops the process, and awaits/cancels the stderr task.

claims.why: The final return in _parse_typed_event wraps unknown event types in AgentMessage with role='system', which is not the default model role.

claims.text: one-shot CLI profiles do not expose a portable approval protocol
claims.why: Both approve and reject unconditionally raise NotImplementedError.

claims.text: session {session_id} exceeded {session.timeout_s} seconds
claims.why: The timeout check uses remaining = timeout_s - elapsed; when remaining <= 0 it stops the process and raises TimeoutError with that exact message.

claims.text: session {session_id} not found
claims.why: If session is None or stdout is None, RuntimeError is raised with that exact message.

claims.text: exit code is captured and reported
claims.why: exit_code = await process.wait() and SessionEnded(exit_code=exit_code) are present.

claims.text: stderr is captured and truncated to last 4000 chars
claims.why: stderr = (await session.stderr_task).decode(...).strip() and SessionEnded(stderr=stderr[-4000:]) are present.

claims.text: events are published in both system and output directions
claims.why: Started is published with direction='system', parsed events with direction='output', ended with direction='system'.

claims.text: the stream yields started, then events, then ended
claims.why: yield started appears before the loop; events are yielded inside the loop; yield ended appears after the loop.

claims.text: blank lines are skipped
claims.why: if not line: continue is present after rstrip().

claims.text: line decoding is lossy but does not crash
claims.why: decode('utf-8', errors='replace') is used.

claims.text: text format returns TextDelta for each line
claims.why: if self._config.output_format == 'text': return TextDelta(text=line) is the first branch.

claims.text: JSON parse failure falls back to TextDelta
claims.why: except json.JSONDecodeError: return TextDelta(text=line) is present.

claims.text: non-dict JSON falls back to TextDelta
claims.why: if not isinstance(data, dict): return TextDelta(text=str(data)) is present.

claims.text: event_type is taken from 'type' or 'event'
claims.why: event_type = str(data.get('type') or data.get('event') or '') is present.

claims.text: typed events are parsed via _parse_typed_event when event_type is non-empty
claims.why: if event_type: return self._parse_typed_event(data, event_type) is present.

claims.text: result field becomes AgentMessage
claims.why: if 'result' in data: return AgentMessage(content=str(data['result'])) is present.

claims.text: content field becomes TextDelta
claims.why: if 'content' in data: return TextDelta(text=str(data['content'])) is present.

claims.text: fallback is TextDelta of the JSON dump
claims.why: return TextDelta(text=json.dumps(data)) is present.

claims.text: text/content_block_delta/assistant_text produce TextDelta from text or delta.text
claims.why: text = data.get('text') or (data.get('delta') or {}).get('text', ''); returns TextDelta if text is non-empty, else None.

claims.text: assistant events extract text blocks from content list
claims.why: For event_type == 'assistant', content list is filtered for type == 'text' and joined; returns AgentMessage if text non-empty else TextDelta of dump.

claims.text: result/turn.completed produce AgentMessage from result/message/usage/data
claims.why: content = data.get('result') or data.get('message') or data.get('usage') or data; returns AgentMessage with string or json.dumps.

claims.text: tool_use/tool_call/tool_requested produce ToolRequested
claims.why: ToolRequested is constructed with name/arguments/call_id from the data.

claims.text: tool_result/tool_completed produce ToolCompleted
claims.why: ToolCompleted is constructed with call_id/result/is_error.

claims.text: bash/command/shell/command_execution produce CommandOutput
claims.why: CommandOutput is constructed with command/output/exit_code.

claims.text: message/assistant_message/response produce AgentMessage
claims.why: content = data.get('content') or data.get('text') or ''; returns AgentMessage(content=str(content)).

claims.text: interrupt sends SIGINT only when process is still running
claims.why: session.process.returncode is None is checked before send_signal.

claims.text: _stop_process terminates, waits 5s, then kills if needed
claims.why: process.terminate(); wait_for(process.wait(), timeout=5); on TimeoutError process.kill() and await process.wait().

claims.text: terminate pops session and sequence, stops process, and awaits stderr task
claims.why: session = self._sessions.pop(...); self._sequences.pop(...); await _stop_process; if not stderr_task.done(): await wait_for(stderr_task, timeout=1) except TimeoutError: cancel().

claims.why: No self-referential assertions or tautological branches found in this chunk.

claims.text: a refusal with no reachable repair: approve/reject raise NotImplementedError with no alternative path
claims.why: The methods unconditionally raise; no other code in this chunk offers a way to approve or reject.

claims.text: a rule inverted with respect to its own stated goal: none
claims.why: No such inversion found in this chunk.

claims.text: a value parsed from output whose format is not pinned: event_type extraction uses 'type' or 'event' with no schema validation
claims.why: The parser relies on ad-hoc keys and falls back to TextDelta or system AgentMessage; if a producer changes the shape, it silently reports a generic TextDelta instead of signalling 'unreadable'.

observations.what: The parser's fallback for unknown event types is AgentMessage with role='system'; for JSON parse failures it is TextDelta. This means malformed or unexpected output is never surfaced as an error, only as a different event type.
In _parse_typed_event for 'assistant', if content is a list but contains no text blocks, it falls back to TextDelta(json.dumps(data)), which may leak raw JSON to the user.

The timeout check uses remaining computed from monotonic clock; if the readline returns quickly, the loop recomputes remaining each iteration, which is correct but may spin if stdout is a stream that returns empty lines quickly.
terminate() does not await process.wait() after _stop_process; it only awaits the stderr task. The process may still be terminating when terminate returns.
The stderr task is awaited with a 1s timeout and then cancelled; if the task is not done, cancel() is called but not awaited, so cleanup may be incomplete.

risks: lines 325-341 and 382-383 | medium | Parser silently converts malformed output into TextDelta or system AgentMessage instead of surfacing an error, making protocol drift invisible. | Add a strict schema check or a distinct 'unparseable' event.
